notes: Deutsch is on for families: every story game in German (no computer voice in German yet; your own recordings still play). A translation can now go live before its voices. In Indonesian, a line whose clip does not load is no longer read by the phone's own voice, which sounded strange and could stop the music on an iPhone

Deutsch is on for families: every story game in German (no computer voice in German yet; your own recordings still play). A translation can now go live before its voices. In Indonesian, a line whose clip does not load is no longer read by the phone's own voice, which sounded strange and could stop the music on an iPhone

Languages: long texts now switch language too (some stayed English), 'All topics' and the sound buttons translated, the game count gone from the language choice, and the coming-soon cards in German, Indonesian and Malay (drafts)
Bahasa Melayu: every story game and the site's buttons drafted, for a native speaker to check (seen only with ?lang=ms)
Musa in Bahasa Indonesia and German (drafts, for native speakers to check); every story game now drafted in both

Less to read for parents: every topic in For parents, and each story's For parents box, now shows the main thing first; the rest is folded under short headings, nothing taken out. What's new shows the latest change, with earlier ones a tap away. The note for parents on Musa 5.5 is now shown.

The two computer voices have names: Aunty Salma (warm and gentle) and Uncle Sani (calm and steady). Each story's 'tell this story in your own voice' opens the page-by-page recorder. For parents → Your voice is shorter to read: the main things first, the rest a tap away.

Musa, a new page 5.5: Musa never forgot the family who fed him as a baby, and looked after the Children of Israel, so it is clear why he calls one of the men in 6.1 his own people (from Ibn Abbas and Ibn Ishaq in al-Tabari's commentary). A draft note for parents gives the sources.

Recording your voice, made simple: Record a story in your voice, one page at a time with its picture (from each story's For parents, or any page's note); My recordings shows how much of each game is in your voice; add your other phones by scanning a code, with nothing to type.
On iPhone, every recording came back empty (“Nothing was recorded”): fixed. The microphone is now opened fresh for each recording and closed after.

Recording your voice: every line now says clearly where it stands: Recording with a timer, Saving…, Saved, sent to your other devices, too short, or what went wrong and what to do; the play button says whether it plays your recording or the computer voice.
Recording your voice works again on iPhone: it records in the iPhone's own format, never waits for ever while saving, and says Saving…, then Recorded on this device, or what went wrong.
Follow Asmau on TikTok: a button at the foot of the home page, beside YouTube and LinkedIn.
Privacy: Asmau now counts, on its server only, how often each game's pictures and voices are downloaded and from which country, never by whom; the privacy note says so.
Yusuf 1.3: Yaqub is drawn dark-skinned like everyone in the prophets' stories. For parents → Who is shown, and how now says how each kind of story is drawn.
Notes for parents on every page of every game: all 558 that were waiting are now shown, and Yusuf 1.2 to 1.5 as you edited them.
The folded line says “📖 Note for parents” on every page that has one, and the first time a small pointer shows grown-ups where to tap.
Each game has a parents’ guide: every note on one page, from the note itself or For parents → Where the stories come from.
The site no longer links to GitHub; the licence names it instead.
Plainer words at the foot of the home page: the name Asmau and its logo are ours.
Write to us: hello@asmau.org at the foot of the home page and in For parents, and on every story page a link to report a mistake on that page.
Clearer follow buttons for YouTube and LinkedIn, and readable links at the foot of the home page.
Follow Asmau on YouTube and LinkedIn: links at the foot of the home page.
Yusuf 13.3: the family bows, everyone drawn dark-skinned, Benjamin bowing with his brothers.
Pictures: everyone drawn dark-skinned in Yusuf 2.4, 2.11, 9.3, 10.4, 11.4 and Musa 12.4, 21.5; Yusuf 11.9 has all ten brothers again.
Yusuf, pages 10.7 and 10.8: Yusuf and the servant are drawn dark-skinned, like everyone in the prophets' stories.
A wrong link now shows a clear 'page not found' page instead of an empty one.
The copyright holder is named: Mohammed Sadat Abdulai.
Asmau's licences: the code is open (AGPL-3.0); the stories, pictures and voices may be shared for free, never sold (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).
Asmau now has its own address: asmau.org. Opening the old address takes you there, with your family code, voice and place.
Yusuf, chapters 10 to 13: Benjamin is now drawn as a teenager, since many years have passed.
Yusuf, page 9.5: a new picture. Yusuf is the right size and the brothers face him as one of them answers.
Two more names on the Great Muslims coming-soon list: Abdullah Quilliam of Liverpool and Muhammad Asad. Games you can play now come first; the coming-soon ones follow.
Seven new names on the Great Muslims coming-soon list: Fatima al-Fihri, Rumi, Ibn al-Nafis, Yunus Emre, Gazi Husrev-beg, Abdul Sattar Edhi and Mariam Alolo.

Yusuf, chapter 9: a new page tells how Yusuf learned about his youngest brother (the brothers told him about their family), so asking for him makes sense; a new picture, both voices, and a draft note for parents with the sources
Yusuf, page 8.3: the king on the throne is the same king as on 8.2
Yusuf, page 5.5: the master of the house looks the same as on every other page (he had a grey beard here)
Yusuf, page 5.3: the master of the house looks as he did when he first took Yusuf home (he looked younger)
Yusuf, page 4.2: a new picture, Yusuf carried among the bundles of goods ('They hid him like a piece of merchandise', 12:19); a draft note for parents gives the scholars' explanations
Yusuf, pages 3.3 to 3.5: Yusuf's hair is short and neat, as in his other pictures
Yusuf, page 2.3: gentle living effects on the new picture (birds, leaves, dust)
In every game, a chosen answer is read to its end before the explanation starts (longer answers, such as Yusuf 2.12, were cut off)
Yusuf, page 2.3: a new picture: the brothers whisper their plan at home among the tents, while Yusuf plays by his father (it looked as if they had already gone out)
Refresh fixes a stuck device without deleting downloaded games (they are kept, and not downloaded again); a separate link deletes them to free space

Updates keep everything a family has on the device and bring a story back to the same page ("Asmau was updated, tap to carry on"); the family code can be shown and copied again in the recorder; Asmau asks the browser to keep its storage
Easier to find: the language of the stories, from a 🌐 button at the top of the home page, on the front of For parents, and in each translated game's For parents box
Easier to find: who reads the stories (a woman's or a man's voice) is now on the front of For parents, in Sound and volume, and in each story's own For parents box
Clearer stories: 29 pages that began with an unclear he or she now say who is meant (Umm Ayman, Nana Asma'u, Musa, Ibn Battuta, Rahmah, Nuh, Yusuf), read again in both voices
After a wrong answer, the explanation stays on screen until the child answers again, and a tap says it again (it used to vanish as soon as it was read)

Bahasa Indonesia: families can now choose it in For parents (Bahasa · Language). Rahmah El Yunusiyyah plays in Indonesian, words and both voices, checked by a native speaker; other games stay in English for now.
Languages: families can choose another language once a game is checked in it (Bahasa Indonesia first; Rahmah's draft waits for a native speaker). One shared story kit for every story game.
Umm Ayman, pages 6.1 and 6.2: she is shown at about forty-five, her age when the Prophet married Khadijah
Umm Ayman, page 6.5: she married Zayd after her first marriage had ended; the note for parents says what the sources do and do not tell
Steadier offline lists: they no longer change depending on the computer that builds the release
Built for many more games: the site downloads far less; games are kept as they are played, and parents can download a whole game (with its size) and delete it to free space
Home page: search, folding sections, covers that load as you scroll; Without internet shows each game's size and state
New game: Rahmah El Yunusiyyah, the girl from the mountains of Sumatra who opened a school for girls in 1923, never gave up, and was honoured by al-Azhar
A man's voice to choose: in For parents, pick a woman's or a man's voice for the lines you have not recorded; your own recordings still play first
Without internet, a device saves only the voice its family chose
New game: Ibn Battuta, the young man from Tangier who travelled for nearly thirty years, from Makkah to China and Mali, told from his own book
New game: Umm Ayman, the Abyssinian woman who looked after the Prophet ﷺ from his birth, in 11 chapters from Sahih Muslim, al-Bukhari and Ibn Sa'd
Living pictures: a soft breeze where the Prophet ﷺ is present; he is never drawn
New game: the story of Prophet Nuh, in 11 chapters with 45 pictures, from Surah Hud and Surah Nuh
Parents' notes for Nuh from Ibn Kathir, al-Bukhari and the Shia narrations of Hayat al-Qulub
Living pictures: stars twinkle in the night sky, lamps and fires flicker, water shimmers, leaves fall and birds cross the sky, placed on each picture
Tapping games: new things to tap never land on top of each other
Sound: tap a sound button (music, sounds, voice) to make it a step louder; after the loudest it turns off; a ring shows the level
Tap & Say and Count with Me: grown-ups press and hold the 🔊 in the corner to change the sound while playing
For parents: every page has its own note, easy to edit
Adam: the matching and ordering games in chapters 3, 4, 8 and 11 show their cards again (they were hidden behind the picture); also Musa's prayer in chapter 11
A grown-up check before any link that leaves Asmau (the verse links, Ko-fi, GitHub): a quick sum for parents
Much smaller first visit: each game downloads when it is first opened (under 1 MB to start), and parents can save every game at once for a journey
Bigger pictures, words and buttons on tablets
On small phones the story words no longer hide behind the buttons
A new, natural voice for every game: a soft West African woman's voice, in English and Arabic (your own recordings still replace it). A new look: the Asmau writing board as the app icon and logo.
Each page shows its number on the For parents line (page 2.3 = chapter 2, page 3)

New: the story of Adam, 11 chapters from Sunni and Shia sources (its pictures are being drawn; for now its pages show icons)
New: Tap & Say for little ones: five pages of words in English and Arabic, and a Find it game
Yusuf: his prayer in the well. Musa: al-Khidr, the green one, and the boy who was kind to his father. Notes from Shia sources in both
Tap & Say has a West African page: the Tabaski ram, the kettle for wudu, the pen, the Ramadan drum, the turban and sandals
New: the story of Adam, 11 chapters, from Sunni and Shia sources (pictures are coming; for now each page shows icons)

Yusuf: the right number of brothers in 24 pictures (ten older brothers, then Benjamin with them)
Every page now has its own picture: 27 new pictures in Yusuf, Musa and Nana Asma'u
Nana Asma'u's walk: she faces the way she walks, and looks like herself
New covers: Yusuf with his hair as in the game, and baby Musa in the basket
Yusuf: a new picture of Yaqub with Yusuf and his little brother

New story: Nana Asma'u, the scholar and teacher this site is named after, in 11 chapters. Its pictures are still to come
For parents: a short home with one page per topic; recording your own voice, in any language, comes first, then privacy and support
A way to record your voice now shows on the front page and on each story's first page
Three sound switches (music, sounds of the place, voice) and volume sliders for parents; the background sounds are a quarter quieter

Yusuf: the brothers persuading their father, the women at the banquet, the brothers' own rule, the eldest's vow and other missing links in the story; his hair and the torn shirt now match in every picture
The stars, sun and moon now bow in chapter 1; the chapter list closes again with a second tap
Musa: the story reads more smoothly, with long pages split in two

Yusuf and Count with Me now use the same clearer voice as Musa
New story: Musa, in 25 chapters with about a hundred activities, its own music, background sounds and a clearer voice. Its pictures are still to come
Six new kinds of activity in the story player, and scenes now have gentle background sounds and movement
New game for the littlest ones: Count with Me (ages 1½ to 4), made for touch screens

Smoother play: Skip only shows after a quiet moment, the question comes back after a wrong answer, the lamp forgives a slipping finger, puzzles have a peek button
